records.title: Recover exact-head CI after consolidated RLS hardening
fix(media): fail closed on unplayable camera previews across browsers
records.source_body:
## Stacked P0/P2 browser/media reliability fix

Depends on draft #508; this branch contains #508's exact source commit and is temporarily targeted at `main` to run the required main-targeted browser-quality CI. The combined diff MUST NOT be merged ahead of #508's approval; once #508 lands, reconcile/rebase and review the narrowed patch.

### Root cause and production fix
- CI WebKit reports `canvas.captureStream()` but is not guaranteed to yield a playable, dimensioned camera preview. The previous code awaited `video.play()` indefinitely, kept permissioned media tracks live and left "Take photo" hidden.
- Camera startup now rejects empty video-track streams and requires a completed playback with nonzero dimensions before exposing the photo action. A 4s deadline fails closed: all tracks, timers and preview state are released; original local-file workflows remain available.
- Browser/OS permission denials retain their explicit status.

### Test/CI improvements
- Browser fixtures check the actual product outcome (ready preview vs visible denial), not API existence.
- Delayed OS prompts use deterministic fake stop-capable tracks so the revocation and late-arrival tests do not depend on browser-specific canvas capture semantics; no test is skipped.
- The mock-clock timeout test advances the preview-start deadline explicitly.
- Each Chromium/Firefox/WebKit lane still runs all browser contracts independently, with `--workers=1` to avoid local server contention.

### Verification
Source syntax compiled with JS parser for both changed JS files. Exact-head Playwright/WebKit/Firefox/Chromium, full SONARA CI, and browser artifact review remain required. Do not merge #508 or this stacked PR until all mandatory gates pass. The current P0 capability inventory generation failure remains separately unresolved and is not masked.

### External references
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLMediaElement/play
- https://playwright.dev/docs/test-assertions
- https://playwright.dev/docs/test-webserver

No production migration/deploy, payments, customer data, camera permission, provider activation or mobile store release.

records.title: Revoke browser grants from reviewed server-only tables
records.source_body:
## Purpose

This is deliberately stacked on PR #513 rather than main. Current main is red after the 18-PR integration merge, so database hardening must not bypass exact-head recovery.

Live Supabase review found 66 RLS-enabled public tables with no policy. That finding is not automatically a vulnerability: many are intentionally server-only. The actionable second-layer gap is narrower.

Exactly 13 reviewed server-only tables still expose broad table DML privileges to both `anon` and `authenticated`, even though RLS/no-policy currently denies rows. This migration removes that unnecessary dependency on RLS always remaining correctly enabled.

## Migration

Adds `20261008110000_revoke_browser_grants_server_only_tables.sql`.

Targets only:
- audit_logs
- billing_events
- db_health_snapshots
- platform_jobs
- prompt_templates
- sonara_control_plane_checks
- sonara_launch_settings
- sonara_realtime_channel_registry
- sonara_storage_bucket_registry
- sonara_ui_capability_registry
- sonara_webhook_verification_registry
- sonara_worker_job_registry
- sonara_write_api_registry

The migration:
- requires every target to exist, have RLS enabled and have zero policies;
- permits only two browser-DML preflight states: all four DML grants (the live drift being repaired) or none (a clean fresh replay already hardened by default privileges);
- aborts on partial grant drift;
- revokes all table privileges from `anon` and `authenticated`;
- proves every browser table privilege is gone afterwards;
- proves `service_role` retains SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE;
- creates no policies, drops no tables and mutates no customer rows.

## Evidence integration

- existing privilege-hardening tests extended; no new Mocha test file added;
- migration checksum pinned;
- generated migration counts advanced 163 → 164;
- replay-safe precondition prevents production drift from breaking clean database replay.

## Merge/deploy boundary

Do **not** retarget or merge this into main until PR #513 is green and accepted.
Do **not** apply this migration to Supabase until its eventual exact-head main commit is green.
This PR performs no live database change.

Remove the 25 now-obsolete ALTER POLICY statements; do not weaken existing migration rules. Keep a narrowly scoped duplicate `subscriptions` SELECT policy proof inside BEGIN ... ROLLBACK, with pre/postflight identical-expression checks and strict 25-policy postconditions.

records.title: security(release): restrict production secrets to consuming GitHub Actions steps
records.source_body:
## P0: reduce production secret scope in the controlled release workflow

**Root cause:** The controlled production workflow declared `VERCEL_TOKEN`, `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID`, and `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD` at `jobs.validate-migrate-deploy.env`. Every step, including third-party dependency installation, compilation, tests and security scans, inherits these credentials after environment approval, although those steps do not require production access.

### Code changes
- Keep only non-sensitive Vercel project routing identifiers and public health URLs in job-level environment.
- Inject each protected secret explicitly through step-level `env:` on **only** the protected credential preflight and actual consuming steps. Eight consuming/preflight steps receive least-privilege assignments; build/test/lint/scan do not.
- Preserve protected production environment, exact-SHA and required-job evidence gates, credential preflight, provider checks, rollback, migrations and approval order. Do not emit credentials in logs, artifact files or GITHUB_ENV.
- Add two regression tests to the existing `tests/exact-sha-job-attestation.test.js` (no new Mocha file): job-level environment has zero `secrets.*`, every credential has an exact reviewed allowlist of receiving steps, and release checks precede credential access.

### Evidence
- Repository source inspection identified job-level secrets and actual step consumers.
- Read-back of committed workflow verified **zero job-level secrets**, 34 preserved named steps, and the intended exact per-secret step scopes. JavaScript test source parses successfully.
- **Additional isolated execution:** 11/11 existing and newly added test callbacks passed when the committed CJS verifier and committed tests were executed in an isolated V8 harness against the committed workflow source, with mocked file reads and GitHub API. This does **not** exercise native Node/Mocha, real GitHub Actions runner YAML parsing, CI or production secrets. Full exact-head checks must still pass and the workflow must be independently reviewed before merge.

### Dependency and rollout boundary
This branch includes draft #516's release-job attestation improvements. Its PR targets `main` so the complete candidate receives required CI; do not merge ahead of independent review and reconciliation of #516 or ignore any red status. No deployment, migration, provider credential retrieval, Stripe action, production website reactivation, or customer data mutation took place.

### Research
- GitHub step-scoped secret injection: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/use-secrets
- GitHub workflow syntax and env inheritance: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax
- Required GitHub environment reviewer protections: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/deployments-and-environments

Owner still needs branch/ruleset enforcement and independent production-environment approvals, issue #460.

### Adversarial regression proof
The isolated 11-case harness passed on the candidate workflow. Three injected regressions were then evaluated: (1) reintroducing a job-level Vercel token failed the job-secret test, (2) adding that token to dependency installation failed the step allowlist test, and (3) removing Supabase access token from the migration dry-run step failed the consumer completeness test. This demonstrates the two new assertions detect both exposure and missing credentials. It remains a synthetic harness, **not hosted CI or full Mocha**.

records.title: fix(billing): shared SONARA subscription destination for all studios
records.source_body:
## Problem
Shared SONARA `GET /billing` previously redirected into `/business-builder/billing`, which requires Business Builder workspace access. Creator Studio and Growth Studio billing links both point to that shared route. Even an otherwise legitimate Creator-only or Growth-only customer could be sent through the wrong workspace.

The Stripe Billing Portal likewise returned all customers to `/business-builder/billing`.

## Implemented
- `GET /billing` is now a first-class SONARA account-level page behind `requireCustomer`. It renders the existing server-side organization-scoped billing summary and `billingPanel` for all three products, without a Business Builder-only gate.
- Retains the existing `/business-builder/billing` page for backwards compatibility.
- Stripe Customer Portal `return_url` and local redirect fallback point to `/billing`.
- Adds tests for authenticated shared billing with no paid workspace, Creator/Growth entry-route redirects, and actual portal request `return_url`.
- Documents acceptance, remaining security/CI gates, and the restricted nature of a portal return URL.

## Files
`server.js`
`tests/server.test.js`
`docs/engineering/SONARA_SHARED_BILLING_CUSTOMER_FLOW_2026-10-08.md`

## Verification status
JavaScript syntax validated for changed `server.js` and test file. **Integration Mocha, full generated inventory, and exact-head GitHub CI not yet green**; do not merge based on syntax verification alone.

## Required merge order and conflicts
- This PR branches from `main` at `9d141e68d1ec14c037f92d1eebb3c2718d583c0a`.
- Canonical origin hardening PR #555 also edits `server.js`. Review and integrate #555 first, then reconcile this PR on the new `main` without dropping the URL guard; do not blindly auto-merge.
- `pnpm run verify:capability-map` and `pnpm run verify:handoff` may require regenerated artifacts after changing the GET /billing route semantics. Regenerate and review exactly, not by hand.
- Require full exact-SHA release matrix, protected main, tenant isolation, a Stripe sandbox portal session and customer plan lifecycle proof.

## No production action
No production deploy, site restoration, live Stripe session, migration, customer data mutation or merge. Preserve the intentional offline state and the owner's release controls.

security(billing): deny one-time Stripe receipts for subscription entitlements
records.source_body:
## P0 — Stripe payment-mode Checkout must never grant recurring subscription access

### Verified vulnerability

A signed `checkout.session.completed` or `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded` event with `mode: payment` and `payment_status: paid` could previously create an active `billing_entitlements` row for any `metadata.plan` string, including `workspace_monthly`, `all_three_monthly`, or `team_monthly`. Payment-mode one-time receipts must not unlock recurring subscription plans. Webhook signature verification alone does not enforce the plan catalog's fulfillment mode.

### Implementation

- `lib/sonara-billing.cjs`: check paid one-time session ID, organization, plan metadata; require the canonical `STRIPE_PLANS[plan].mode === "payment"` and reject quoted/retired plans **before any purchase or entitlement write**. Deny unrecognized recurring/free plans with `checkout_plan_mode_mismatch`, missing paid metadata with `checkout_metadata_missing`.
- Keep subscription-mode Checkout completion separate from `customer.subscription.*` fulfillment, and defer unpaid one-time sessions until actual paid events.
- `tests/billing-delivery-reliability.test.js`: explicit regression for monthly/annual recurring plans, missing/retired/free keys, missing metadata, successful future catalog-approved one-time SKU, failed persistence retry, unpaid and subscription-mode Checkout.
- `docs/security/STRIPE_CHECKOUT_MODE_ENTITLEMENT_BOUNDARY_2026-10-09.md`: threat model, compatibility, historical-payment reconciliation and release proof.

### Evidence and limitations
- Syntactic compilation: changed billing and test file **passed**.
- Isolated dynamic execution with a real loaded canonical plan table and mocked PostgREST calls: **15/15 assertions passed**.
- **Full Mocha, exact-head CI, real webhook sandbox, payment/cancellation and multi-tenant RLS are NOT certified.** No provider account mutation or live payment action performed.
- Current catalog has **zero** self-service plans with `mode: payment`, so automatic one-time fulfillment correctly stays blocked. A future one-time SKU requires its own merchant, rights, refund and provider proof.
- Unsupported historical paid events should be reconciled manually; 503 retry and alert until reviewed, not silently marked fulfilled.

### Merge gates and overlap
- [ ] Run `pnpm exec mocha tests/billing-delivery-reliability.test.js`, `pnpm run verify:launch` and exact-head green GitHub matrix.
- [ ] Inspect `lib/sonara-billing.cjs` conflict with **draft #555** (canonical origin / truthful billing state); integrate both guards deliberately rather than overwriting one.
- [ ] Check **draft #558** for shared billing navigation compatibility.
- [ ] Verify Stripe test-mode payment/subscription events, signed webhook paths and retries, paid access enforcement, tenant rejection and reconciliation.
- [ ] Require protected main, human review, independent release approval and rollback evidence.

No merge, production deploy, database migration, website restoration or real-money activity.

Stripe API contract: https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create ; https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks

### P0 follow-on: ownership proof before webhook state mutation
- Added `verifyWebhookCustomerBinding(config, customerId, organizationId, userId)` in `lib/sonara-billing.cjs`. It uses the existing `stripe_customers` table (unique Stripe customer ID) to authorize the **customer-to-organization relationship** before any subscription, purchase or entitlement write.
- Check the subscription's `customer` against the original tenant metadata and stored customer mapping. One-time paid Checkout additionally checks `metadata.user_id` when present. No inbound webhook may create or infer a new mapping.
- Fail closed on missing customer ID, missing/duplicate/mismatched ledger rows, failed lookup and malformed JSON. Webhook HTTP handler will 503 for a retry/reconciliation rather than silently acknowledge unauthorized fulfillment.
- Added adversarial cases to `tests/billing-delivery-reliability.test.js`; updated existing signed webhook, subscription history, generation-period and HTTP retry fixtures with customer-binding proof.
- **Isolated test harness:** 10 relevant actual regression callbacks passed. **Syntax:** 5/5 changed JS files pass. These are not project Mocha or hosted CI.
- **Operational risk:** older subscription records without a mapping may now retry. Review and reconcile those customer records through Stripe sandbox and tenant database before merge; do not fabricate mappings from webhook metadata. Explicitly verify canceled-subscription revocation and RLS.
- Research: Stripe metadata is informational, not an authorization mechanism: https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata

records.source_body:
## Scope
Two bounded, source-backed corrections plus one staging-only diagnostic improvement to exact-head release gates, separate from product PRs #574, #576 and #577.

- PR #577 `verify:source-licence`: false-positive reading of `open-source XcodeGen` in the iOS README.

Used current GitHub source plus exact-run job logs; verified the README no longer matches the source-license checker’s permissive-license pattern, and the handoff count matches the configured Mocha discovery on main. **No Node 24/pnpm full test run has been performed locally.** Full workflows must pass on this PR's exact head; draft and no merge/deploy until all release checks are green.

### Explicitly unchanged
No source-license relaxation, no toolchain changes, no new runtime deps, no workflow skip, no database changes, no direct pushes to main, no provider activation, no live website deployment.

### Release notes
Base `main` is currently unprotected; enable strict required status checks, PR approvals and bypass restrictions through authorized repo administration, and verify the enforcement with a rejected red merge.


## Subsequent exact-head repair after observing actual CI
- Prior head `7e562212...` completed with **Node Runtime Compatibility and SONARA One Validation successful**; full `SONARA Industries CI` still failed at `verify:capability-coverage`.
- GitHub runner log identifies `61 formula definitions` in the generated coverage document versus **59 actual definitions** imported from `lib/sonara-formula-library.cjs`. Verified current formula table already enumerates those same 59 keys, then corrected only the stale summary number in `docs/CAPABILITY_ROUTE_SCHEMA_COVERAGE.md`.
- Fixed replay runner's `result.stderr || result.stdout` evidence loss: P1 staging drift diagnostics now include a bounded pipe-delimited subset of stdout plus stderr, preserving the nonzero fail-closed result and not dumping stdout from other probes.
- Added regression assertions to the existing native-migration-replay infrastructure test file (4 targeted workflow checks passed in a JS harness). Generated test file count remains unchanged.
- The **25-policy drift is still not repaired**; authoritative native PostgreSQL proof on the newest head is required to identify the mismatched attributes. No migration/grant changes, no merge or deploy.


## Read-only connected preview RLS evidence (2026-10-09)
Connected Supabase preview project `yqncsonkxgwhcxedgevk` reports PostgreSQL 17.6. A read-only SQL comparison against the exact 25 expected named P1 policies returned **0 missing**, **16 changed role sets**, **25 changed USING expressions**, **21 changed WITH CHECK expressions**, **0 changed policy commands**. This is the **preview database**, not the ephemeral CI replay; it must not be used as an automatic migration authority. Some changes represent already-optimized `auth.uid()` expressions or restricted `{service_role}` policies. No DB writes, migrations, grants, policy rewrites or production updates were made. See dated audit doc.


## October 10 exact-head follow-up: no authorization relaxation
- Previous head `c500b83e...` finished **7/9 workflows successful**, with `SONARA Industries CI` stale generated industry formula rows and `Native migration replay` 25 outdated P1 policy expectations.
- Regenerated all 40 industry formula rows in canonical source order, including previously omitted `activation_rate` and `retention_rate`.

Replaced the **staging-only** test with an exact snapshot of current restrictive roles: 21 `{service_role}` all-command policies with `true` predicates, and four `{authenticated}` owner-only optimized `SELECT` policies.

No change to migration history, grants, RLS policies, production, or connected preview.

After the rolled-back duplicate-policy trial, the replay runner makes a **new psql connection** and independently asserts the two original identical subscription SELECT policies still exist. It fails CI if this post-rollback catalog check fails. This is real PostgreSQL acceptance logic, not a comment asserting rollback. records.title: fix(ci): verify post-hardening RLS policies in native replay
records.source_body:
## Release-gate repair, isolated from product code

The native PostgreSQL replay currently aborts at "P1 policy definition drift on 25 policies" on exact-head PRs, including #609. The repository's last migration `20261008100000_tighten_service_role_rls_policies.sql` intentionally hardened 21 pure service-role policies to `TO service_role USING (true) WITH CHECK (true)` and optimized four authenticated `auth.uid()` ownership checks. The old P1 temporary SQL probe was still expecting all 25 pre-hardening definitions and would attempt to rewrite them backwards.

This review-only fix:
- Checks all **25** policy names, commands, scope, permissiveness and exact post-hardening shapes; 21 must be role-scoped service_role/TRUE and four must retain the `user_id` owner comparison.
- Aborts on widened applicability, missing policies, legacy per-row `auth.role()` checks or a nonidentical subscription policy pair.
- Tests that dropping exactly one identical subscription SELECT policy is safe **inside a rolled-back transaction**, then verifies the original pair was restored.
- Corrects stale verifier commentary. **No migration, production SQL or customer records are changed.**

Requires the full native replay matrix (Node 22/24/26 and PostgreSQL 16/17/18), other mandatory CI, and exact SHA review. Keep DRAFT; do not merge/deploy/relax RLS checks simply to obtain green.

### Additional independent source-license gate repair
- `ios/README.md` now describes XcodeGen as an **external project generator**, not as a licence for SONARA source. Prior word choice triggered the proprietary-source scanner despite the repository remaining `UNLICENSED`; no source licence or proprietary protection changed.
- This addresses a second CI blocker observed on the baseline product PR. The WebKit browser regression and generated capability inventory remain independently gated and are **not** suppressed here.


### Follow-up evidence, not a green claim
- The initial post-hardening fixture passed its 25-policy audit but failed at the **subscriptions duplicate preflight** in native PostgreSQL replay. A diagnostic-only exception now prints the exact two source policy definitions on the next replay; it still fails closed.
